rows.text: Glarb turns the top of your library into a second hand — but only for lands and for spells costing four or more. That restriction is why the deck is deliberately top-heavy, and why the surveil matters more than the deathtouch: you look, and if the top card is too cheap to cast off it, you bin it. Everything you bin then feeds a graveyard the deck is fully equipped to use.

rows.name: Glarb, Calamity's Augur
rows.text: three mana, deathtouch, permanent access to the top card, and lands plus mana-value-four-and-up spells can be cast straight off it. Tap to surveil 2 — that is how you fix a bad top card AND fill the yard, every single turn.

Anything with mana value three or less on top of your library is dead. Surveil it away. This is the single most common mistake with this deck: leaving a Brainstorm on top and losing a whole turn of free casts.

rows.name: Bilbo, Thief in the Night
rows.text: spells cast from anywhere other than your hand cost {1} less, which is a discount on every single card you cast off the top. He also recasts an instant, sorcery or artifact from your graveyard on every attack.

rows.name: Planetarium of Wan Shi Tong
rows.text: whenever you scry OR surveil, look at the top card and cast it for FREE, once each turn. Glarb surveils every turn by himself, so this is a free spell per turn cycle, and it ignores the mana value floor entirely.

rows.name: Sensei's Divining Top
rows.text: sets the top three, and cashes itself in for a card when the top is bad.

rows.name: Scroll Rack
rows.text: swaps a hand of expensive cards you cannot cast for cards off the top — and then puts the expensive ones back on top where Glarb CAN cast them.

rows.name: Noxious Revival
rows.text: puts any card from any graveyard on top of your library. If it costs four or more, Glarb casts it immediately, at instant speed, for one green mana or two life.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep ramp and a land drop engine. Glarb costs three, but the deck's payoff is casting five- and seven-drops off the top, so Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Nature's Lore and Exploration are what make those turns happen.

Surveil at the end of THEIR turn, not yours. Glarb's tap ability is free information and free graveyard filling — do it on the last opponent's end step so you know your draw and your top-of-library cast before your turn begins.

rows.name: Glarb, Calamity's Augur
rows.text: deathtouch on a 2/4 means he blocks almost anything, so he survives more often than he looks like he should. Still, hold up Legolas's Quick Reflexes or Misdirection when the table has a removal spell up — losing him costs you two cards a turn.

rows.name: Planetarium of Wan Shi Tong
rows.text: six mana is a lot, but with Glarb out it is a free spell every turn for the rest of the game. Prioritise it over any single creature.
